requirement_text.ISS-0329: auth_pipeline_configurable_verifier_test.exs:140 hardcodes idp_realm_id causing cross-partition unique constraint collision. Fix: use unique_realm/1 + dynamic Application.put_env for :oidc_jit_provisioning with on_exit cleanup. Test-code only change.

task.description:
HARD GATE. Independently validate lib/letflow/design/iss0329-jit-disabled-realm-unique.md against ISS-0329's 8 acceptance criteria and WF-03 Step 2 requirements. Read the design artefact directly -- do NOT rely solely on CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary.

Check each acceptance criterion explicitly:
1. Names exactly one file to change: test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_configurable_verifier_test.exs
2. Explains why unique_realm/1 alone is insufficient (JitProvisioningConfig.default/1 enabled: true fallback)
3. Specifies Application.put_env pattern for :oidc_jit_provisioning with on_exit cleanup
4. States the config mutation must precede insert_tenant_for_realm!
5. Explicitly scopes out: config/test.exs, lib/, scripts/test_parallel.sh
6. Notes auth_pipeline_test.exs:131 (bpm-default) is tracked as ISS-0108, out of scope
7. Notes test_parallel.sh exit-code concern is retracted
8. No compilable Elixir code in the design artefact (only @spec + prose)

Also verify: the design is unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement from. The fix pattern must be complete: what lines change, what the config mutation looks like (shape of the map entry), where on_exit goes, ordering relative to insert_tenant_for_realm!.
acceptance_criteria: All 8 criteria verified against the actual design artefact
Design is unambiguous enough to implement from (no gaps in the fix pattern)
No implementation code present in the design

summary.verdict: PASS — all 8 acceptance criteria satisfied; design is unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement from.

criteria.1_single_file: PASS — Section 4 (Scope Boundary) names exactly one file as CHANGE: test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_configurable_verifier_test.exs. No other file is listed as CHANGE.
criteria.2_naive_swap_insufficient: PASS — Section 2 explains the exact failure chain: for_realm/1 reads the config map, Map.fetch/2 misses on the generated realm, falls through to default/1, which returns enabled: true, causing JIT to succeed and the pipeline to return HTTP 200, failing the assert conn.status == 403.
criteria.3_put_env_on_exit_pattern: PASS — Section 3.3 Steps 2–4 (prose only) specify: read Application.get_env into original_jit_config; register on_exit to restore via Application.put_env; then call Application.put_env with a map containing the unique realm keyed to %{enabled: false, default_status: :active, default_roles: []}. The config map shape is stated explicitly in Step 4 and repeated in Section 7.
criteria.4_config_before_insert: PASS — Section 3.4 states the ordering invariant explicitly in a diagram: put_env(add realm) → insert_tenant_for_realm! → call_pipeline. Section 3.3 Step 5 also calls this out in prose as a required ordering.
criteria.5_explicit_scope_exclusions: PASS — Section 4 Out of Scope table lists config/test.exs, lib/letflow/oidc/jit_provisioning_config.ex, any other file under lib/, and scripts/test_parallel.sh — all three required exclusions are present.
criteria.6_iss0108_bpm_default: PASS — Section 5 explicitly notes auth_pipeline_test.exs:131 uses hardcoded 'bpm-default', states it is already tracked as ISS-0108, and declares it out of scope for this fix.
criteria.7_test_parallel_retracted: PASS — Section 6 explicitly states the exit-code concern 'has been retracted as a misread of the script' and confirms no change to scripts/test_parallel.sh is needed.
criteria.8_no_compilable_code: PASS — All function references in Section 3.2 are @spec signatures only (no def/do/end bodies). Section 3.3 uses numbered prose steps. Section 3.4's ordering invariant is ASCII pseudocode, not valid Elixir. No compilable code blocks are present anywhere in the document.
criteria.clarity_check: PASS — The config entry shape (%{enabled: false, default_status: :active, default_roles: []}) is stated in both Section 3.3 Step 4 and Section 7. Affected line (140) is identified. The three new statements are described in order. on_exit placement (before the put_env mutation) is explicit. ELIXIR-DEV has a complete, unambiguous specification.
